manualReview.summary: Selected both-sex aging effects agree with the registered sex-adjusted endpoint
manualReview.note: GEO provides a raw-count matrix and a reanalyzed archive of per-sample count files. Table S1 mouse_sample_info reconciles all 36 author-used 6- and 27-month hypothalamus samples (8F/8M young, 10F/10M old) to the 36 registered libraries by library ID, age and sex, with no exclusions on either side. The authors fit each sex separately (edgeR filterByExpr/TMM, limma log2CPM, all ages as groups); Table S2 lists age-related genes (>=1.5-fold at any age, BH P<0.05, BIC trajectory filter) per sex. Because each age group has the same sex composition, the registered additive-sex coefficient targets the equal-weight mean of the within-sex age effects. Within the declared scope of 246 hypothalamus genes listed in both sexes, 241 pair with the registered output (97.97%): Pearson r=0.995957, Spearman 0.991571, 241/241 signs agree, median absolute log2FC difference 0.0315. Five listed genes are absent from the registered tested table. Sex-specific listed genes, the nonsignificant tail and pooled inference remain outside this scope. Evidence and reproducible extraction are in continued-sources/GSE314817/turbo-2026-11-15-partial2/.

concordanceReview.note: Table S1 shows that the registered and author endpoint cohorts are the same 36 animals, with 8 female and 8 male at 6 months and 10 female and 10 male at 27 months. With the same sex composition in each age group, the additive-sex age coefficient is a weighted average of the female and male within-sex age effects with equal weights. The equal-weight mean of the author per-sex 27-versus-6 log2FC therefore estimates the same biological contrast in the same units. It is exact for linear models and approximate for the NB GLM. The comparison is restricted to genes listed in both sexes, where this mean is defined. Separate per-sex filtering and variance modelling are estimator and inference differences. This review does not equate P values or FDR calls.

manualReview.summary: Author maturation TF effects agree with both registered P21-vs-P0 contrasts; diet contrasts remain exploratory
manualReview.note: The official normalized CPM matrix is accessible, supports the registered P0/P21 and diet axes, and was rehashed locally (SHA-256 bce4b726...). Authors ran edgeR on raw counts that were not deposited and emphasized P0-to-P21 maturation within chow and HFD. The only supplementary file, mmc1.pdf, contains Supplementary Table 1: 227 transcription factors DE during maturation in either diet, with signed fold changes and FDR for CD0vsCD21 and HFD0vsHFD21. Coordinate-based extraction recovers all 227 rows. Within this selected TF scope, p21_vs_p0_chow pairs 223 genes (Pearson r=0.998204, Spearman 0.998717, 222/223 signs agree) and p21_vs_p0_hfd pairs 223 (Pearson 0.998265, Spearman 0.998443, 221/222 nonzero signs agree); Glmp, Kmt2a, Ybx3 and Zfp638 are unmatched. The P21 HFD-versus-chow and P0 HFD-versus-chow results remain valid labeled exploratory contrasts on the deposited matrix with no author comparator. Evidence and reproducible extraction are in continued-sources/GSE135639/turbo-2026-11-15-partial2/.

datasets.summary: No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: The only quantitative hypothalamic author result is Npy (fold change 5.88, FDR 0.0024); the Nature supplement inventory has no complete or selected hypothalamus DE table. One gene is far below the author-concordance-v2 minimum of 30 paired genes, so no scoped comparison is valid. The existing author-method DESeq2 refit is a separate reconstruction and does not verify the registered edgeR-QL output.

No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: The recorded Cell Metabolism supplement contains figure/category summaries only, with no gene-level same-contrast DE table (selected or full). No paired gene effects exist, so no scoped comparison can reach 30 pairs.

No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: The retained publisher Tables S1-S3 hold prefrontal-cortex interaction, sex and genotype results; S4-S6 are enrichment tables. None provides hypothalamus genotype effects, so the tissue (cohort) and contrast are incompatible with the registered hypothalamus comparison. The paper's hypothalamus result is a significant-gene count and Ube3a direction only.

No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: Author Tables S5/S6 report JTK_CYCLE rhythmicity, phase and amplitude run separately per diet. They contain no diet-effect coefficient, so the effect definition is incompatible with the registered common diet main effect. Any comparison of JTK statistics with the diet logFC would be invalid.

No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: The paper codes age ordinally across 6/18/27 months and fits four overlapping time-domain slopes. Those coefficients are not algebraically equivalent to the registered 27-minus-6 endpoint, so the contrast and effect definitions are incompatible and no scoped comparison is valid.

No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: The exact 467-cell author cohort is reconstructed, but the paper publishes no global sex-DE table. Source Data Figure 2 supplies cluster/cell IDs used for cohort selection, not per-gene sex effects. No paired author sex effects exist.

No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: Author Data S1/S2 are cluster-specific DE tables (asinh fold changes, detection fractions) computed on 20,194 QC-retained cells. The registered output is an all-captured-cell (28,410 barcodes) animal pseudobulk. The analysis unit, cell membership and effect definition (asinh cluster FC vs log2 pseudobulk FC) are incompatible, and no barcode/cluster map exists to rebuild matching tracks.

No valid author-concordance-v2 scoped comparison: The author analysis uses 254 Crh+/Snap25+ neurons selected by clustering, with no published retained IDs or cluster map. The registered output aggregates all 602 deposited cells, so cohort membership is incompatible with any author Crh-neuron result. Three of 514 initially QC-qualifying cells also remain unidentified.
